## Overview

[Ark.jl](https://ark-ecs.github.io/Ark.jl/stable/) is an entity component
system (ECS): a `World` holds entities, each entity is a set of components
(plain immutable structs), and the model's behaviour is written as functions
("systems") that loop over queries such as "every entity with an `Aphid`
component". `ArkBackend` keeps the state of a cellular automaton in such a
world, so that mobile agents written as entities can share it.

This vignette writes the aphid-borne virus of the previous vignette in ECS
style, then uses the one-entity-per-cell mode to let a scouting system tag
diseased plants with a component and rogue them later. It ends by comparing
the cost of the agent backends.

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using CellularAutomataCore
using Ark
using Plots
using Random
using Statistics
```

## The crop

The crop is the same cellular automaton as before: healthy (0), latent (1) and
symptomatic (2) plants, with slow spread by root contact.

```{julia}
crop = LocalRule(VonNeumann(1)) do cell, nbrs, ctx
    if cell == 0
        k = count(==(2), nbrs)
        return bernoulli(ctx, 1 - (1 - ctx.p.ε)^k, 1) ? Int8(1) : Int8(0)
    elseif cell == 1
        return bernoulli(ctx, 1 / ctx.p.τ, 2) ? Int8(2) : Int8(1)
    end
    return cell
end

n = 80
u0 = zeros(Int8, n, n)
for (i, j) in ((20, 20), (60, 30), (40, 65))
    u0[i, j] = 2
end
p = (ε=0.02, τ=5, inoculation=0.4, acquisition=0.6, loss=0.1, flight=3,
     emigration=0.03, immigrants=40)
prob = CAProblem(crop, u0, 90, p; seed=1)
```

## Aphids as entities

An aphid is an entity with one component, holding its position and whether it
carries the virus. Components are immutable, so a system that changes an aphid
writes a new component in its place.

```{julia}
struct Aphid
    pos::NTuple{2,Int}
    viruliferous::Bool
end
```

The behaviour is three systems. A flight lands on one of the cells exactly
`flight` cells away (in the maximum norm), as Agents.jl's `randomwalk!` does on
a grid, so this is the model of the previous vignette. The world holds a `Xoshiro` random number
generator as a resource, seeded from the problem's seed, and the systems reach
the crop through `read_cell(world, pos)` and `write_cell!(world, pos, value)`.
Entities cannot be removed while a query over them is running, so emigrants
are collected first and removed afterwards.

```{julia}
function arrive!(world, k)
    rng = get_resource(world, Xoshiro)
    for _ in 1:k
        new_entity!(world, (Aphid((rand(rng, 1:n), rand(rng, 1:n)), false),))
    end
end

function emigrate!(world, p)
    rng = get_resource(world, Xoshiro)
    leaving = Entity[]
    for (es, aphids) in Query(world, (Aphid,))
        for i in eachindex(es)
            rand(rng) < p.emigration && push!(leaving, es[i])
        end
    end
    foreach(e -> remove_entity!(world, e), leaving)
end

function fly_and_probe!(world, p)
    rng = get_resource(world, Xoshiro)
    f = p.flight
    ring = [(dx, dy) for dx in -f:f for dy in -f:f if max(abs(dx), abs(dy)) == f]
    for (es, aphids) in Query(world, (Aphid,))
        for i in eachindex(es)
            a = aphids[i]
            pos = mod1.(a.pos .+ rand(rng, ring), (n, n))
            plant = read_cell(world, pos)
            if a.viruliferous && plant == 0 && rand(rng) < p.inoculation
                write_cell!(world, pos, 1)
            end
            carries = plant == 2 && rand(rng) < p.acquisition ? true :
                      rand(rng) < p.loss ? false : a.viruliferous
            aphids[i] = Aphid(pos, carries)
        end
    end
end

function aphids!(world, p, t)
    emigrate!(world, p)
    fly_and_probe!(world, p)
    arrive!(world, p.immigrants)
end
```

`ArkBackend` takes the component types of the mobile agents (the world must
know them when it is created), an `init!(world, p)` that creates the first
aphids, and an `update!(world, p, t)` that runs after each sweep of the crop
with the new time.

```{julia}
backend = ArkBackend(:grid; components=(Aphid,), init! =(w, p) -> arrive!(w, 1500),
                     update! =aphids!)
sol = solve(prob; backend, saveat=30)
plot([plot(sol; snapshot=i, c=[:palegreen, :orange, :darkred], clims=(0, 2),
           colorbar=false, title="day $(sol.t[i])") for i in eachindex(sol.t)]...;
     layout=(1, 4), size=(950, 270))
```

This is the same model as the Agents.jl version, but the two draw their random
numbers in a different order (here all emigrants are chosen before any aphid
flies), so they agree in distribution, not run by run. The fraction of plants
infected at day 60, over 40 runs, can be compared with the untreated histogram
of the previous vignette:

```{julia}
day60 = EnsembleProblem(remake(prob; tspan=(0, 60));
                        output_func=(s, ctx) -> (count(>(0), final_state(s)) / n^2, false))
runs = solve(day60, Synchronous(), EnsembleThreads(); trajectories=40, backend,
             save_everystep=false)
(mean=mean(runs.u), sd=std(runs.u))
```

`agent_model(integ)` returns the world, for callbacks or for inspection.

```{julia}
integ = init(prob; backend)
step!(integ, 30)
world = agent_model(integ)
carriers = count(a -> a.viruliferous,
                 (a for (es, aphids) in Query(world, (Aphid,)) for a in aphids))
(aphids=count_entities(Query(world, (Aphid,))), carriers=carriers)
```

## One entity per plant

With `ArkBackend(:cells)` every plant is an entity with a `CACell` component,
which holds the plant's linear index and state. The run is the same as with
the grid:

```{julia}
cellular = ArkBackend(:cells; components=(Aphid,), init! =(w, p) -> arrive!(w, 1500),
                      update! =aphids!)
solve(prob; backend=cellular, saveat=30).u == sol.u
```

Because plants are entities, systems can query them like any other entity and
give them components of their own. Here a scout walks the field once a week,
finds each symptomatic plant with probability one half and tags it with a
`Flagged` component recording the day. Three days later a crew rogues every
flagged plant, which becomes an empty cell (3) that neither infects nor can be
infected. The rogue system writes the new state straight into the plant's
`CACell` component, and the next sweep of the crop reads it from there.
Components are added outside the query, as entities cannot change while one
runs.

```{julia}
struct Flagged
    day::Int
end

function scout!(world, t)
    t % 7 == 0 || return
    rng = get_resource(world, Xoshiro)
    found = Entity[]
    for (es, plants) in Query(world, (CACell{Int8},); without=(Flagged,))
        for i in eachindex(es)
            plants[i].state == 2 && rand(rng) < 0.5 && push!(found, es[i])
        end
    end
    foreach(e -> add_components!(world, e, (Flagged(t),)), found)
end

function rogue!(world, t)
    for (es, plants, flags) in Query(world, (CACell{Int8}, Flagged))
        for i in eachindex(es)
            t - flags[i].day >= 3 && (plants[i] = CACell(plants[i].index, Int8(3)))
        end
    end
end

managed = ArkBackend(:cells; components=(Aphid, Flagged),
                     init! =(w, p) -> arrive!(w, 1500),
                     update! =(w, p, t) -> (aphids!(w, p, t); scout!(w, t); rogue!(w, t)))
rogued = solve(prob; backend=managed, saveat=5)
```

```{julia}
untreated = solve(prob; backend, saveat=5)
infected(s) = [count(∈((1, 2)), u) / n^2 for u in s.u]
removed(s) = [count(==(3), u) / n^2 for u in s.u]
plot(untreated.t, infected(untreated); label="infected, untreated", lw=2,
     xlabel="day", ylabel="fraction of plants", legend=:topleft)
plot!(rogued.t, infected(rogued); label="infected, scouted and rogued", lw=2)
plot!(rogued.t, removed(rogued); label="rogued", lw=2, ls=:dash)
```

```{julia}
plot(rogued; snapshot=length(rogued.t), c=[:palegreen, :orange, :darkred, :white],
     clims=(0, 3), colorbar=false, title="day 90, scouted and rogued", size=(400, 380))
```

At day 90:

```{julia}
healthy(s) = count(==(0), final_state(s)) / n^2
(untreated=(healthy=healthy(untreated), infected=infected(untreated)[end]),
 rogued=(healthy=healthy(rogued), infected=infected(rogued)[end],
         removed=removed(rogued)[end]))
```

Roguing keeps the infected plants left standing to about a quarter of the
field, against nearly all of it untreated, but mostly by removing them: well
over half the crop has been rogued, and at the end about one plant in six is
healthy, against one in twenty untreated. With aphids flying in all season, the virus
reaches healthy plants faster than weekly scouting can find the sick ones.

## In continuous time

The crop can also be written as rates and simulated event by event with
`Gillespie()`, the aphids still flying once a day. With an agent backend the
run stops at every whole day for the mobile agents, whose `update!` sees the
day as an integer, exactly as after each step in discrete time. Here a plant
is infected by each symptomatic neighbour at the rate that gives the daily
probability `ε`, and becomes symptomatic at the rate that gives `1/τ` a day:

```{julia}
crop_rates = EventRule(VonNeumann(1)) do cell, nbrs, ctx
    cell == 0 && return (-log(1 - ctx.p.ε) * count(==(2), nbrs) => Int8(1),)
    cell == 1 && return (-log(1 - 1 / ctx.p.τ) => Int8(2),)
    return ()
end
continuous = EnsembleProblem(CAProblem(crop_rates, u0, 60.0, p; seed=1);
                             output_func=(s, ctx) -> (count(>(0), final_state(s)) / n^2,
                                                      false))
cruns = solve(continuous, Gillespie(), EnsembleThreads(); trajectories=40, backend,
              save_everystep=false)
(discrete=(mean=mean(runs.u), sd=std(runs.u)), continuous=(mean=mean(cruns.u), sd=std(cruns.u)))
```

The two agree closely, with a mean of about 0.32 of the plants infected at day
60 in both: the daily probabilities of root contact and of symptoms are small,
so a day is a small step for them, and the aphids act once a day in both.

## Choosing a backend

Without mobile agents every agent backend gives exactly the result of
`ArrayBackend`, because they all sweep the same array engine. What differs is
where the state is kept between steps, and so the overhead. Here are 50 steps
of Life on a 200 × 200 torus:

```{julia}
using Agents: Agents
life = CAProblem(Life(), rand(Xoshiro(1), Int8[0, 1], 200, 200), 50)
backends = [ArrayBackend(), AgentsBackend(:grid), AgentsBackend(:cells),
            ArkBackend(:grid), ArkBackend(:cells)]
labels = ["ArrayBackend()", "AgentsBackend(:grid)", "AgentsBackend(:cells)",
          "ArkBackend(:grid)", "ArkBackend(:cells)"]
reference = final_state(solve(life; save_everystep=false))
all(b -> final_state(solve(life; backend=b, save_everystep=false)) == reference, backends)
```

```{julia}
ms_per_step(b) = 1000 * minimum(@elapsed(solve(life; backend=b, save_everystep=false))
                                for _ in 1:3) / 50
[label => round(ms_per_step(b); digits=3) for (label, b) in zip(labels, backends)]
```

In `:grid` mode the agent backends cost nothing over `ArrayBackend`. In
`:cells` mode each step also gathers the cells into an array and scatters them
back, which for a rule as cheap as Life costs several times the sweep itself;
for a rule that does more work per cell the difference shrinks. Use `:cells` when the cells themselves need to be agents
or entities: to give them components, query them alongside other entities, or
use Agents.jl's tools on them.
